question: When two tangents, PA and PB, are drawn to a circle from a point P outside the circle, and the angle between them is 90°, what is the distance from P to the center (O) of the circle, if the radius is 5 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the angle between two tangents from an external point is 90°, the tangents and the radii to the points of contact form a square.

The side of this square is exactly equal to the radius of the circle (r = 5 cm).

The distance from the external point to the center is simply the diagonal of this square.

Distance OP = r × √2 = 5 × √2 = 5√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5√2 cm.**
